name: The Four Tenets of AI
author: Joshua Almeida
rule: Each tenet has to be as low as possible.

tenets.name: Cost
tenets.measure: USD, tokens, or compute-seconds per answer

tenets.name: Bridge
tenets.definition: Glue/integration hops connecting AI to the real world (APIs, tools, translation layers).
tenets.measure: integration hops / tool calls per task

tenets.name: Work
tenets.definition: Steps, retries, and loops to reach a result.
tenets.measure: steps and retries per task within a fixed budget

tenets.name: Theory
tenets.definition: Unproven assumptions and unverified claims the system relies on.

ladder.summary: exact -> finite -> infinite -> deciding what's enough

levels.name: Bit
levels.definition: The smallest exact value: one light, lit or dark (active-low: lit = 0, dark = 1).

levels.name: Local
levels.definition: One finite machine; nothing outside it, no network hops.

levels.name: Pi
levels.definition: Pi (3.14159...) is infinite, never-ending, non-repeating; no computer can hold it exactly, only round it.

levels.name: Tenets
levels.definition: Cost, Bridge, Work, Theory decide how many digits are enough. More precision costs compute (Cost bit); trusting a rounded value unchecked raises the Theory bit. Goal 0000 = AI online.
